system.name: FlashTrace
system.one_liner: Efficient multi-token attribution for reasoning LLMs: whole spans are attributed in one pass and importance is traced recursively back through the reasoning chain to the input.

content.variant_note: two lanes split by a dashed vertical line draw the same isometric token sequence with different arrows, above a row of three small measured charts
content.argues: Token-by-token attribution is slow and lets reasoning tokens soak up importance; span-wise recursive attribution reaches the input in K hops and stays fast up to 10K tokens.
content.subject: Isometric token cubes (input, reasoning, output) with attribution arrows for the naive and the span-wise scheme, plus three small result charts.

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw baseline and method in the same token-strip grammar so that only the arrows differ: a fan of thin per-item arrows with a clock and its cost formula versus a few fat span arrows with lightning bolts and the lower cost. Back the claim with a row of three small measured charts underneath.
lessons.suits: Efficiency or faithfulness papers whose baseline cost or failure can be shown as a pattern of arrows over a token sequence, with measured evidence beneath.

evidence: Motivation for FLASHTRACE. Top: Naive token-bytoken attribution requires expensive per-token computation, while FLASHTRACE performs efficient span-wise recursive attribution.
Naive multi-hop attribution scales poorly with reasoning length, while FLASHTRACE remains efficient even for 10K tokens.
Finding 1: Reasoning tokens absorb the majority of attribution mass.

summary: FlashTrace explains the output span of a reasoning LLM by tracing importance back through the chain of thought to the input, attributing a whole span in one pass instead of one token at a time. Figure 1 is a motivation figure. The top half draws the same token sequence twice in isometric view (white input cubes, light-blue reasoning cubes, dark output cubes), split by a dashed vertical line: on the left a fan of thin cyan arrows from every output token with a clock and a Θ(|O|×|I+T|) cost; on the right two fat gradient arrows hop span by span, with lightning bolts and Θ(K|I+T|). Below, three small charts show that reasoning absorbs attribution weight (19% to 7% left for the input), that recovery of ground-truth inputs drops from 26% to 9%, and that baseline time climbs to about 280 s while FlashTrace stays flat.
summary_zh: FlashTrace 按 span 一次性归因并沿推理链递归回到输入。图 1 上半部用同一条等距立方体 token 序列对比逐 token 归因与 span 级递归归因，下半部三张小图展示推理吸走归因权重、输入召回率下降和基线耗时暴涨。
notes: The first chart has no colour key: cyan = share left for the input and grey = share absorbed by reasoning tokens are read from the caption (about 80% to over 90% on reasoning tokens). The (a)/(b)/(c) letters occur only in the caption, not in the figure. Prior labels kept (side-by-side-contrast first) but the bottom row is a finding-cards style row, hence contribution-mosaic as third kind; the cube count of 24 is approximate.
